newsitem.title: ITALY: Boskin sees less chance of U.S. rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Boskin sees less chance of U.S. rate rise.

text.p: The chances of the Federal Reserve Open Market Commmittee tightening monetary policy on May 20 have diminished because of an improved outlook, former chairman of U.S. Council of Economic Advisers Michael Boskin said.
"I think two or three weeks ago people would have said for sure that they (the FOMC) will raise rates on May 20," Boskin told a news conference in Milan in response to a question from a reporter.

"Now it's probably fifty-fifty on May 20 and there is probably one more move...unless sentiment about the economy changes," Boskin said, adding "if you look at long term interest rates they have backed off by 25 basis points."
Boskin said he did not believe the Fed had initiated what would prove to be a series of interest rate hikes comparable to the sequence of increases in the late 1980s or in 1994.
"This time so far there has been one (interest rate rise) and there was widespread speculation it would be one of several, maybe three or four," he added.
The Fed raised the federal funds rate by one quarter of a percentage point on March 25 to 5.50 percent.
"They will probably take out a little more, either in May or July, but I do not anticipate it unless the economy starts heating up," he said.

"The economy in the last few weeks has shown signs of slowing to a more moderate pace from four to four-and-a-half percent in late 1996 and early 1997 down to the two to three percent range," Boskin added. Milan newsroom +392-66102321
